1

Details

What each workstream answered, one line each (details on the slides):

  1. t0 (F1, F2, F5, F6): the start time of the charge is one DAQ latency for the whole bench, ~300–340 ns; fixing it improves position by 4–31 %.
  2. Drift velocity uncertainty (F8): the quoted ±0.07 µm/ns was statistics only; the real spread is 2 % (det2/3) to 5–8 % (det4/6/7), because the gas changed during runs.
  3. w0 (F9): a mechanical tilt of the chamber against the telescope, measured independently from positions.
  4. Steep tracks read shallow (F4, F18, F21): a selection cut plus a bowed chamber; a position map fixes 1–27 % of the resolution. A ~2 % residual is unexplained.
  5. SPS (F14, F18, F20): a 256-ADC offset bug voided the old SPS fits; head-on RAW data fix the prompt footprint σ0 at 0.32 mm (Y) and ≤ 0.29 mm (X).
  6. Physics floor (F3): a toy says 0.30–0.35°, set by diffusion; we measure 3–6× that.
  7. Dead strips and x–y charge balance (F12, F15): two kinds of fault (chamber vs electronics); the charge balance is not a gain problem.
  8. SPS drift velocity (F16): the old 14 % was the fit's depth grid; v(243 V/cm) = 14.1 µm/ns from the column duration; an 8 % slope deficit remains (local gap or fit, not separable).
  9. One reconstruction (F22, F7, F10, F11, F13): no per-dataset switches; finds 1–5 % more tracks.

Ledger: rerun/model_audit/FINDINGS.md; each workstream's report: rerun/model_audit/ws_*/REPORT.md.

What the fit does, and which handle each finding touches

Side view of one chamber: a cosmic muon ionises the 30 mm gas gap; the strips record when and where the charge lands

What the reconstruction fits, per chamber view:

t0: when the charge starts

p0: where the track crosses the mesh

w / v = the angle

σ0, D: how wide the charge is

Hover any dotted word or data point for its definition and numbers. Details under each slide carry the method and caveats.

2

Details

The reconstruction (wft/) fits each view's strip waveforms with a forward model: the track's charge is cut into depth slices (60 ns bins), each slice is spread by diffusion and the strips' resistive-layer sharing, and the fit adjusts t0, p0 and w (plus per-slice charges) to match the waveforms. The angle is tan θ = w / v with v the chamber's calibrated drift velocity. The bench reference is the M3 telescope (four planes, ~0.4 mm pointing).

The calibration bundle per chamber and run condition carries v, the RC kernel, σ0 and Dp, w0/kw (angle offset and scale against M3), the dead-strip list and t0 information.

t0 floated: an earlier t0 draws the same line

Left: two (t0, p0) pairs give one line; only the modelled cloud width differs. Right: per-event χ² vs t0 (det3), side minima one 60 ns bin away

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_t0/REPORT.md

3

Details

F6. Charge in bin k sits at time t0 + u_k and position p0 + w·u_k. Moving t0 later and p0 along the track by w·Δt0 reproduces the same line: the only things that pin t0 are the growth of the diffusion width with depth and "no charge arrives before the mesh". So the free t0 wanders ±53–140 ns per event, with side minima one 60 ns bin away; the reported t0 error of 1–2 ns is meaningless, and because p0 slides with it, positions of inclined tracks suffer.

The old ±5 ns prior on t0 was invisible: next to χ² ~ 10⁴ it carried no weight. Source: ws_t0/REPORT.md.

t0 is one DAQ latency; pinning it improves position

Left: earliest charge on the strips, every golden chamber. Right: held-out tracks, pinned t0 vs free t0

4

Details

F1: yes, one latency. All golden rows use the same DREAM configuration and the scintillator trigger. The fine timestamp ftst is the trigger phase in the 60 ns clock (−10 ns per class, measured −7.7…−12.0), so t0 = C − 10 ns·ftst. C measured fit-free (earliest 30 % pulse crossing, phase-corrected), X / Y: det2 300/309, det3 319/327, det4 334/339, det6 323/327, det7 304/304 ns. No X–Y FEU offset.

Pinning at C − 10·ftst (1320 held-out tracks per chamber): mesh position vs M3 improves 4–31 %; angle s68 within ±0.03°; χ²/dof rises 4–20 % (model error the free t0 had absorbed). A scan of C shows the angle scale moves +5 % per 100 ns of C and matches the timing v on all ten planes at C ≈ 300–330 ns: the old stored t0s were too late, which is the +2…+5 % ladder shift of F6.

F5: once t0 is pinned, the x–y t0 coincidence checks nothing. Compare column mid-times (t0 + u50) instead: they centre at 0 with no table. Not yet implemented.

Never pin on n_TOF: there the trigger is not the particle. Code: wft/calibrate.py measure_latency, set_w0kw.py --latency-cache --pin-t0. No bundle uses the pin yet.

5

DetailsF8: you were right, ±0.07 µm/ns (0.2 %) was too small. Three different numbers:
  1. Error on the run-mean v: ±0.16–0.27 µm/ns (0.4–0.7 %) for det2/det3, ±0.4–1.2 for det4/6/7. Includes time-block bootstrap, estimator and window choice, and the M3 angle scale (~0.25 %, irreducible).
  2. Local spread around it, which is what matters when v is used elsewhere: 1.7–2.1 % (det2/3), 5–8 % (det4/6/7). In time: det4 −9…−10 % over its day run, det6 +12 %, det7 +4 % over the shared night. The independent column-duration route moves the same way (right panel), so the gas really changed.
  3. +tan vs −tan agree to ≤ 1 % (det6 Y 2.7 %); the apparent 2–7 % came from a biased head-on offset in fleet_tables.py, still to fix.
det3 X vs Y differ by +2.1 ± 0.4 % on the same events. The sign changes between chambers (det4 −3.0 %, det6 +1.9 %), so it is not strip-layer geometry; it is an angle-scale error of the size of the width–tilt trade. On the bench kw absorbs it; elsewhere it is a 2–3 % per-view systematic.

w0 is the chamber sitting tilted on the bench, measured twice

Left: what w0 is. Right: angle offset from the fit vs tilt from position residuals alone, 16 chamber views

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_v_w0/REPORT.md

6

Details

F9. w0 is the fitted lateral speed w for a track that M3 calls perpendicular, i.e. an angle offset α = w0/v. Negative is not unphysical: it is a direction. A tilted chamber also gives a position residual that grows with tan × position, which measures the same tilt from positions alone. The two agree (r = 0.81 over 16 chamber views); rms offset 0.34° → 0.18° after subtracting the position tilt. det6 Y −0.86° vs −0.89°. det3 moved to the bottom slot (6-25) changed its offset with the mounting.

Sign: every Y offset is negative (−0.27 … −0.89°): the bench slots are not level along M3 x. Fixed by M3's z axis pointing up (upper plane at 1302 mm), an external fact.

The apparent det3 field dependence was an artefact of set_w0kw.py; as an angle it is constant (−0.28 / −0.24 / −0.28° at 1000 / 700 / 500 V).

Risk: bench w0 is mounting, so it must not be used at n_TOF. The n_TOF bundles were bench transfers including w0/kw; which w0 stage 3 actually used is not checked.

Most of the steep-track fall was a selection cut

Measured slope / true slope vs M3 angle. Dashed: the F4 analysis (cut on the fitted slope). Solid: no cut, tilt removed

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_widthtilt/REPORT.md

7

Details

F4. 03_angles.py dropped fits with |tan_fit| < 0.08. In the shallowest reference bin that removes exactly the fits that came out too shallow, so that bin is inflated by 3–13 % and the curve appears to fall with angle. Without the cut (w0 removed, ± sides averaged), the steepest bin (|tan| ≈ 0.36) is within 0–6 % of the shallow ones: det7 0, det3 ~1.5, det4 3–4, det2 Y 4.5, det6 X 6 %.

The rest of the fall is the chamber bow (next slide). Toys with the real windows, noise and gains close to ≤ 0.3 % at every angle, so the fitter itself is unbiased on its own model.

The rest is a bow: the tilt varies across each chamber

Left: tilt offset w0 vs position, X view (ramps ±0.6 µm/ns). Right: mesh height from M3 positions alone (points) vs the bow the w0 ramp predicts (dashed)

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_widthtilt/REPORT.md

8

Details

w0 is not constant: on every chamber and both views it ramps from about −0.6 to +0.6 µm/ns over 300 mm, zero near the centre. Through the telescope's acceptance, position and angle are correlated (strongly on det6), so a ramp in position looks like an angle non-linearity.

Independent check from M3 positions only: the mesh-height curvature fitted from position residuals vs tan has the same sign on all 10 chamber views, 120–250 /km (40–200 /km predicted from the w0 ramp), i.e. a 1–3 mm dish. Gravity sag of an edge-supported board is the candidate; which way the centre sits is not pinned.

The bow also biases position by tan × height (~±0.45 mm at tan 0.3), likely part of F14's 0.5–0.76 mm bench position resolution. Bench geometry: never transfer this map to n_TOF.

9

Details

Cross-validated s68 change X / Y: det2 −12/−26 %, det3 −12/−16, det4 −3/−25, det6 −26/−27, det7 −1/−18 %. Code: optional angle_map in wft/calib.py, applied by tan_of() in wft/reco.py; test wft/tests/test_angle_map.py. The map is bundle content, so it fits the single reconstruction. Not yet written into the production bundles.

Residual after the correction: a symmetric compression between |tan| 0.15 and 0.36 of ~2 ± 0.5 % (det3, det4 X, det6 X), 4 % det2 Y, 7 % det4 Y, none on det7. Unexplained. An M3 plane-scale error is excluded only by plausibility (it would need a 5–10 % scale error). Rim bins (< 30 mm from the edge) flip sign on det3 X and det2, unchecked.

The width–tilt trade is real, but only a percent

Left: fitted slope of steep tracks vs the footprint σ0 the model assumes (data). Right: toys, a model wider than the truth compresses ~2 %, mostly at shallow angles

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_widthtilt/REPORT.md

10

Details

F21. On data (det4, det6) changing the assumed footprint σ0 from 0.24 to 0.54 mm lowers the slope 3–10 %, most at shallow angles. No (σ0, Dp) pair on the grid makes the M3 angle the χ² minimum, so the trade is real but percent-level, not the cause of the steep-track compression.

F18. The per-event wide/narrow footprint choice is harmful: in toys a truly wider footprint picked this way is unbiased, but in data the wide-pick fits read 5–15 % shallower even in the chamber centre and are 1.3–5× brighter. With the choice off, bright tracks still read 5–10 % shallower on det6/det7: a brightness-dependent mismatch the model does not describe.

Resolution of the trade: fix σ0 from SPS head-on data (next slides) fleet-wide, drop the per-event choice, and keep the bow correction separate as geometry. Not yet done or gated in the single reconstruction.

Width probes on det2/det3/det7 are still on condor; the data trade rests on det4/det6 only.

12

Details

F20. Run_71 RAW gives truth; zero suppression is emulated on the same events. Treating suppressed samples as measured zeros (they are: the DAQ measured them below threshold): t0 ≤ 27 ns, position 15–27 µm, slope 0.03–0.07 µm/ns from RAW. Censoring them (what F16/F20 used): 44–66 ns, 45–86 µm, 0.14–0.31 µm/ns. The bound treatment sits in between. With zeros measured, ZS recovers σ0_X and Dp_X; it cannot separate σ0 from RC spread in Y. Now the default in the single reconstruction.

Cache bug: the EOS-built ZS caches never subtracted the ZS baseline, so kept samples sat 256 ADC above the suppressed zeros, and RAW rows sat on raw pedestals of 300–700 ADC. Fixed in 7505338. F16 and F20 numbers came from those caches and are void; F16 is redone on the fixed caches (next slides), the 25.64° angle numbers of F20 are not yet.

Also fixed: front-end-dropped RAW samples (23 %) had been fitted as zeros (χ² +30 %); they are now marked missing.

13

Details

F20, the summary. Things set by the strips and electronics (footprint, sharing, pulse shape) transfer. Things set by the gas (drift velocity, diffusion, attachment) do not, because the gases differ. Gain does not.

F14: SPS measured det4's intrinsic resolution at 0° as 176 µm (earlier, 3-pitch method). In this workstream, position minus the uRWELL prediction gives 391 / 311 µm (X / Y) at 0°, upper bounds including a ~250 µm reference term. The bench's ~0.5 mm is consistent with M3 pointing (~0.4 mm) plus angle, plus the bow's ±0.45 mm. At 25.64° the inclined view adds ~0.6 mm in quadrature (pessimistic: censored ZS, low-field plateaus).

The x–y t0 difference on clean RAW head-on tracks has σ 84–118 ns: t0 is uncertain at 60–80 ns per plane, intrinsically.

Still to run: the SPS gate with the measured H4 dead-strip mask; the angle scale and resolution at 25.64° on the fixed caches.

SPS drift velocity, two ways: column duration and ladder

det4 at H4, 25.64° mount. Left: one track. Middle: the summed strip signal lasts T = gap / v. Right: the sideways speed w grows as v·tan θ

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_spsv/REPORT.md

14

Details

F16. The particle ionises the whole gap at once: electrons next to the mesh arrive first, those from the cathode last. Summed over all strips the signal is a box of length T = gap / v, smeared by the electronics, and the angle terms cancel, so T is measured without the track model.

In the tilted view the landing point slides sideways at w = v·tan θ; with a known mount angle, w / tan θ is the "ladder" velocity. The product w·T = gap·tan θ contains no velocity: it checks the gap (or the fit) directly.

The old span route (spread of single-strip hit times anchored to one velocity from run_71) is retired: it was built on combined_hits times, and its anchor carried a field label computed with 30 mm instead of the registry's 28.8 mm.

The old "14 %" was the depth grid; T = 2.05 µs

Left: the old fits' column end sat on their depth-grid end, fixing the ratio. Right: strip-sum waveforms at 243 V/cm with box fits

15

Details

The old F16 fits sized their depth grid (K bins × 60 ns) from the span-route velocity. The fitted column end q_uend sat exactly on the grid end at every plateau (2400, 2520, 2700, 2820, 2880, 2880 ns), so v_span divided by 28.8 mm / q_uend is 1.155–1.167 from arithmetic alone: the "14 %". The "+4 % self-consistency" compared the slope with the grid end, so it measured nothing either. On top, those fits used the caches that sat 256 ADC high.

Model-free column duration at 243 V/cm: head-on RAW (run_71) 1970 ns, head-on ZS (run_63) 2050, 25.64° ZS (run_62) 2040 (Y) / 2130 (X): T = 2.05 ± 0.07 µs. A flat box reads 2–5 % shorter than a box with a charge gradient; the charge falls ~50 % along the column (late charge lost, consistent with O₂ attachment).

Caveats: the box estimator assumes the bench det4 X template holds at H4 (same DREAM registers, not checked further); ~11 % of inclined events are cut by the ±16-strip window (not corrected); run_71 RAW caches use a per-strip pre-window baseline without common-mode correction.

What remains: the slope is 8 % short of gap / T at every field

Left: v(E) from 28.8 mm / T (model-free) and from the fitted slope. Right: the gap implied by slope × duration, which contains no velocity

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_spsv/REPORT.md

16

DetailsAbsolute drift velocity, det4 at SPS (gap / T), µm/ns with 28.8 mm (30 mm): 243 V/cm 14.1 (14.7); 235: 13.5 (14.1); 217: 12.7 (13.3); 200: 11.2 (11.6); 174–182: 9.6–10.4 (10.0–10.8). Defensible: v(243 V/cm) = 14.1 +0.6 −1.1 µm/ns (box estimator, gap 26.5–30 mm, run-to-run). Fields are HV / 28.8 mm; whether the mesh voltage adds to the drift field is not in any record. Residual: the fitted slope |w|/tan is ~8 % below 28.8 mm / T at every field 174–243 V/cm (8 plateaus, 2 runs, both ZS treatments). Equivalently the implied gap is 26.2–27.0 mm. Two explanations, and the existing data cannot split them:
  • the local gap really is ~26.5 mm at the beam spot: det4's bench gap map is unusable (25.5 mm overall, charge quartiles 24.4–33.5 mm), and its ±3 mm bow allows it;
  • the fit compresses tilted tracks: in run_61 at the same field the slope reads 11.38 at 15.465° but 12.67 at 25.64°, which a gap error cannot do (or a ~1.5° error in the 15° mount, or 32-sample truncation).
Consequence: with v = 28.8 mm / T, angles at 25.64° read 8 % low in tan (23.8°). The old +4 % is not the truth; the truth is −8 % ± 3 %, owed to the local gap or angle-dependent compression. Stated limitation. Not a model-width effect: setting Dp and σ0 to the measured SPS values moves the slope ≤ 0.7 % (χ²/dof 7.3 → 5.9).

17

Details

F3, the toy for the paper. Electron by electron: Fischle cluster sizes with δ-ray ranges, Magboltz diffusion, Polya gain, the measured footprint, strip pitch, pulse shape, sampling, noise and ADC ceiling; fitted with the toy's own exact mean model, started at truth. Floor 0.30–0.35° (s68) at every angle 0–45°, all five chambers.

Which physics sets it (det3, 20 ns, one effect off at 5/20/35°, all on 0.34/0.30/0.30): no diffusion 0.02/0.05/0.09, so diffusion is the floor; no cluster-size fluctuation 0.25/0.20/0.19; no gain fluctuation 0.29/0.29/0.24; electronic noise negligible. Closed form σ_θ ≈ D_T √(6(1+f)/(N·G)), N drift electrons, G gap, f = 1/(1+θ_Polya): 0.29° for det3. D_T is the same on all bench chambers, so the floor is too.

The old "~1° physics floor" (script 18, FLOOR_TAN = 0.018) is withdrawn: it assumed 0.30 mm centroid jitter per 60 ns bin; the physical value is 0.185 mm. The measured 1.0° (best chamber) is model error of the charge-dispersion response, not a detector limit.

Red curve: with 60 ns charge bins even a perfect model degrades past 25° and reads steep tracks shallow (−0.5° at 40°), because v·Δt·tan θ exceeds a strip pitch. 20 ns bins fix it. Small on the bench (−0.05° at 20°), the main term for n_TOF pairs at 30–45°. Untested on data. Proposed paper paragraph: ws_floor/REPORT.md. Limits: X view only, bench gas only (n_TOF gas has about half the D_T, so a lower floor; not run).

18

DetailsF12. 17 bench rows, 3 SPS flat sets and n_TOF runs 55/79/145, in strip position. Three tests: census (M3/uRWELL crossing, no hit), flank (silent strip between two strips above 300 ADC) and silent (< 5 % of the neighbourhood's occupancy). Two fault classes, consistent across datasets:
  • Chamber-side, follows the chamber across FEUs: det6 X 0.8–18 mm alternate, 150–186, 342–350; det7 X connectors 0–3 (reappear at n_TOF D on FEU 1); det6/det7 Y 40.6–43.7; det2 X 7.0, 53; det4 X dead stripes (confirmed at SPS).
  • Electronics-side, follows an FEU channel: bench FEU 6 ch 269 (det2/4/7); FEU 4 ch 50 (det3, det6, n_TOF A); FEU 7 ch 307/398/400.
det3's whole bench mask is FEU-7 electronics: moved to n_TOF A (FEU 3) it would censor 3 live strips and miss FEU 4 ch 50. det6/det7 masks miss 15–18 chamber-side strips; det4 over-masks (census statistics at ~30 crossings/channel). n_TOF bundles carry no dead list at all. Rule proposed: chamber faults by position + each dataset's own electronics faults. SPS: det4 at H4 was read on FEU 03, connectors 3–6, so the bench mask by channel number censored the wrong strips. Fixed: CalibrationBundle.remap_channels and an H4 mask measured with the uRWELL. The SPS gate with that mask is not run; the golden mask corrections are not gated.

19

Details

F15: neither dead strips nor missing normalisation. X and Y share one amplification gap, so gain cancels in qx/qy. Per-connector X/Y gains (split-half) are equal to ±2 % (≤ ±5 %); applying them changes the width by ≤ 0.004, and the ln(qx/qy) map in 25 mm cells is flat to 0.02–0.03. Censoring restores dead-strip charge on average but those windows are 1.3–3× wider.

What does drive the width: wrong x–y pairing (det7 0.32 → 0.19 when M3 confirms both views), saturation (16 % of det3 events, 30 % det2, 69 % det6/det7), and censored windows. The residual on det6/det7 tracks their X–Y χ²/dof difference (r 0.44–0.46), a model-side effect of the F4/F18 family.

Consequence for the single reconstruction: pairing tolerance per event class (saturated / censored / clean). Not yet implemented.

x–y t0 window, head-on charge tolerance, angle error floorfrom the bundle's own measurements
zero-suppressed samplesmeasured zeros
WFT_U_FIXEDdeleted
F7: neither hard-coded nor loosened ad hoc. The plausibility window is (0.30–1.60) × 30 mm / v of the bundle (det3 250–1330 ns, det6 375–2000 ns). The old upper edge rejected 7–17 % of M3-confirmed single tracks. Gate: detected +1.12 / +1.15 / +3.70 / +1.85 / +5.45 points (det2/3/4/6/7). On the tracks production already found, s68 improves slightly on every view. Not yet in the single reconstruction (all bundle content, not switches): fixed fleet σ0 and dropping the per-event choice; the pinned t0; per-class pairing widths; the 20 ns grid. The bundles must be re-finalised under the new algorithm before a production pass.

det6's two-track "pairs" were bright single muons

Left: separation of the two fitted tracks. Right: fraction of clean single muons split in two, old and new minimum

Source: rerun/model_audit/ws_unify/REPORT.md

21

Details

The 417 det6 splits were the brightest single muons with the worst χ² (p94–p99), refitted as two parallel tracks ~2 mm apart sharing charge ~40/60: 4.1 % of clean singles on det6 Y. A real two-muon overlay spreads out to 16 mm. With a minimum separation of 4 strip pitches (3.11 mm), false splits are 0.05–0.72 % on every chamber and view, inside the 1 % bound.

Risk: the n_TOF pipeline (wft_beam) inherits the 4-pitch minimum; pair efficiency at small separation there has not been re-measured.

What this does not rule out, and what is left to do

Not explained yet

  • A ~2 % compression of steep tracks after every correction (det4 Y 7 %)
  • Bright tracks reading 5–10 % shallow on det6/det7: a model mismatch
  • Measured angles are 3–6× the physics floor: the response model is the limit
  • Bow and tilt maps are bench mounting; n_TOF needs its own (which w0 stage 3 used is unchecked)
  • SPS: the fitted slope is 8 % short of gap / T, either the local gap or the fit compressing tilted tracks

Decided, not yet in production

  • Fix σ0 fleet-wide (Y 0.33, X 0.24–0.29) and drop the per-event choice: needs its gate
  • Pin t0 on bench bundles; switch the x–y check to column time
  • Per-event-class pairing widths; corrected golden dead masks; dead lists for n_TOF
  • 20 ns charge grid (untested on data)
  • Re-finalise and promote every bundle under the unified algorithm; re-measure n_TOF pair efficiency

22

Details

Condor probes still out: width probes on det2/det3/det7 and toy-mode probes (widthtilt), the X footprint grid on 22 ZS flat rows (ws_sps). The SPS changes did not go through the before/after gate. det7's promoted bundle has empty run conditions (F10; promote_phys.py --fill-conditions fixes it at the next promotion).
